verdicts.claim: 01 obligation: 'detectability anti-join from sensor active ranges + 02's parseability'
verdicts.evidence: One sentence ('sensor active ranges + 02's alert parseability gate the negative universe') that is not operationalized and, read literally, is destructive: FloodNet events start 2020-11-16, so gating the negative universe on sensor active ranges deletes every negative before 2020-11 — i.e. 40 of 57 trigger days. 02's parseability bears only on the alert path at complexes, not on bus stops or cells. Also unused: 02's measured recall (0.970 new era, 0.778 old era) means missed station extractions are FALSE NEGATIVES concentrated in the old era, compounding the pre-2014 confound. And 01's coverage constants give alert holes the draft never carries into its era rules — 2020-04-01..27, flood signal effectively 2016+, and Socrata tail 2026-06-29 vs archiver capture 2026-08-16 (dark 2026-06-30..08-15) — while complexes draw most of their positives from alerts.

verdicts.claim: 01 obligation: 'Calibration expectations anchored: published FIM systems run CSI 0.26-0.45'
verdicts.evidence: Carried verbatim as 01 requires — but the draft repeats it without naming the estimand mismatch, which makes it dishonest as an expectation. Published FIM CSI is computed against inundation EXTENT, where the positive fraction of the evaluated domain is often tens of percent. Here the pooled unit-event base rate is roughly 0.1-0.3%: even Ida, the largest storm on record, gives 857/13,370 = 6.4% of bus stops (measured) and 324/1,336 = 24% of land cells, and typical trigger days are far smaller. CSI 0.26 at a 0.2% base rate demands precision and recall both near 0.4 on a PU-labeled target. As written the anchor either condemns a reasonable model or invites operating-point gaming. State the base rate beside the anchor, and add the base-rate-relative baseline (B0's CSI) as the real floor.

verdicts.claim: DP2: three per-kind L2 logistics with B0/B1 baselines; 'the full model beats B1 on held-out events' is the headline validation claim
verdicts.evidence: The headline is grain-dependent and close to vacuous at two of the three grains. Precip is constant within a Cell-hour, so B1 assigns ONE identical probability to every bus stop in a cell (06: mean 12.9, max 67) and to every complex in a cell — any within-cell feature beats it by construction, and 'the asset layer earns its keep' is decided before a single coefficient is fit. At cell grain B1 and the full model differ only by borough, n_assets and the elevation aggregate. Also missing: the L2 penalty lambda is never mentioned. Tuning it on the same event-grouped folds used for reporting leaks; the draft's 'sweeps inside the folds' names RADIUS_M and the 311 threshold but not lambda. Nested CV or a frozen lambda, and a per-kind statement of what beating B1 would actually mean.

verdicts.claim: DP2: the three fits give independent validation evidence
verdicts.evidence: They do not. One 311 point mints the cell positive AND ~1.7-2.1 bus_stop positives AND (via the entrance OR) the complex positive from the same report. Agreement across kinds is close to mechanical, so three per-kind CSIs are not three independent confirmations and must not be read as such in the write-up. Worse for the cell fit specifically: a cell is positive iff a 311 SJ/SH point lands in it, and criterion (a) makes the DAY an event because the citywide SJ/SH count is high — the cell model's y and the event trigger are the same data stream, so the cell fit mostly learns where people call 311. That is precisely the chronic-reporter channel the with/without-history split is meant to isolate, and it cannot: the history covariates are NFIP + sewer-backup density, not SJ/SH call density itself. Add historical SJ/SH call density to the with/without pair or say the cell model cannot separate the channel.

verdicts.claim: DP3: public number = per-kind percentile index 0-100, probabilities confined to validation tables
verdicts.evidence: Honest under PU labels — but as specified it is not computable, because it inherits the grain hole (next verdict): a percentile of eta requires a per-unit eta, and eta is defined at unit x event. Two further consumer problems: a within-kind percentile is not comparable across kinds, so the serving panel cannot color one map or rank a station against a bus stop; and a percentile is uniform by construction, so half the city is always 'above median' whatever the actual risk. If the index survives, publish the eta->percentile mapping (the empirical CDF) in the coefficient JSON, or ticket 10 cannot render an index at all.

verdicts.claim: DP6 / DP1: gold/flood_exposure = 'one row per scored unit: asset_id, kind, score_index, eta, score_version, frozen_at'
verdicts.evidence: Grain contradiction at the center of the design. The model is fit at unit x EVENT grain on event-varying features — window max mm_1h/3h/6h, window total, antecedent mm_24h, n wet hours, event-side gauge margin, and NFIP/sewer covariates that the draft itself makes time-varying ('strict as-of before each window'). A single eta per unit therefore does not exist until 08 says how event features are marginalized: a frozen reference storm, feature means, or a static-only sub-model. The draft never says. Until it does, the headline table, the percentile index, and ticket 10's 'detector = score x live forcing?' are all undefined — and if the static score already contains precip, multiplying by live forcing double-counts it.

verdicts.claim: DP6: 'Model artifact = the 10 interface... The detector re-evaluates the SAME linear model with live features - no second model to reconcile'
verdicts.evidence: This does not serve ticket 10. Every precip and coastal feature in the fitted spec is an aggregate over the CLOSED event window: 'max mm_1h, max mm_3h, max mm_6h in window; window total; n wet hours' and 'max water-level margin over nws_minor at the assigned gauge in window'. At detection time the window is open, so none of them exist. Feeding running partial-window maxima into coefficients fit on full-window maxima is a different model: every feature is downward-biased at t < window end, the bias shrinks as the event proceeds, and the resulting score is uncalibrated and non-monotone in time. Marking a 'live-computable subset' does not fix it — dropping terms from a fitted linear model changes what the remaining coefficients mean. The cheap fix is already on the rails: pipeline-08 stores mm_1h, mm_1h_prev, mm_3h, mm_6h, mm_24h, n_hours_24h at (src, cell, hour_end_utc) — trailing, leakage-free, identical offline and live. Fit at unit x event-HOUR grain on those columns and define the event score as max over hours; then one linear model genuinely serves both the history table and the detector, and 'no second model to reconcile' becomes true instead of aspirational.

verdicts.claim: DP6: 'score_version = sha1(label_version, features_version, model-constant JSON, scored-universe definition)'
verdicts.evidence: The chain omits precip identity entirely — no src, no AORC/MRMS partition version, no grid sha256 (pipeline-08 stores one per ref/grids row). An AORC re-key, a month rebuild, or a switch of src leaves score_version unchanged, which defeats the exact hazard pipeline-08's Answer spends its length preventing ('srcs are never pooled', src collinear with era). assets_version is correctly inherited twice (via label_version per 06(c) and features_version per 07). Add src + the precip partition/grid hash, and the RADIUS_M/threshold values actually used.

verdicts.claim: DP6: outputs serve the eventual serving panel (absent-key conventions, provenance)
verdicts.evidence: Three holes. (a) No absent-key convention: what is emitted for an asset-less land cell (330 measured), a NoData bus stop, or a complex with zero grade_ok children — NULL score row, missing row, or removed from the universe? Undefined, and it collides with the frozen '445 complexes' given the 'fallback = drop' rule and the 30 single-entrance complexes.
